subject: Error estimate of a function of posterior predictions?

messages.author: 661876c3c8e40896
messages.subject: Error estimate of a function of posterior predictions?
parts:
Hi all,
I am new to this group but have been using INLA for hierarchical spatial modeling for quite some time. I am interested in computing a difference in risks based on estimates derived from INLA. In a standard MCMC Bayesian setting, I would compute the risk difference at each iteration, forming a distribution, and would be able to calculate an associated credible interval around the risk difference. I have used bootstrap resampling of the original dataset, fitting a model in INLA each time, calculating the risk difference (and repeating!). Does anyone know of a better way to estimate the error of a function such as the risk difference? Does the bootstrap seem legitimate even though it can be thought of as frequentist?
Thank you for any and all assistance!
Best,
Melanie
